A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same shortcut-model framework and ESC method. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments, component ablations, convergence curves, and generated samples, including the ESC results in Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds the longer-trained ESC+ ImageNet result in Tables 3 and 6.

M1.justification: The shortcut framework, plug-in velocity, class-consistent batching, gradual time sampler, and training objectives are retained. ESC+ has a longer training budget but no documented new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unconditional CIFAR-10 generation and ImageNet-256×256 generation with class conditioning and classifier-free guidance. ESC+ uses existing coverage.

E2.justification: The additional autoregressive, masked-generation, and diffusion/flow rows in v4 Table 3 already appeared in v1 Table 6 for the same ImageNet comparison. The full comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 adds ESC+ trained for 480 epochs, approximately 2.4 million iterations, alongside the retained 240-epoch ESC configuration. This extends the training-budget setting while retaining the SiT-XL/2 architecture and one-step FID50k evaluation.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 2 and the analyses of sampling steps, class-consistent batching, training stability, and model size in Appendices D–F are retained. The corrected Figure 8 caption does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added ESC+ result follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 6 add ESC+ with ImageNet FID50k 2.53 at 480 epochs. The existing ESC result of 2.85 at 240 epochs and the other benchmark and ablation results remain unchanged; this is an additional result at a larger training budget.

T1.justification: Theorem C.7 explicitly changes its optimality statement to the conditional distribution p(u0,t | x0,t). Appendix A.3 revises the Gaussian noise specification and EDM-to-cosine/velocity derivation, including removal of intermediate normalization equations. The main error bounds and remaining proofs are retained apart from renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract extends its headline performance claim to FID50k 2.53 with twice the training steps, alongside the retained 2.85 result. The central contributions concerning a common design framework, component analysis, and training from scratch remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 3 distinguishes linear conditional paths from their induced marginal velocity fields and qualifies Fisher-information optimality as conditioned on data samples. This narrows the interpretation of the existing analysis; the limitations in Appendix F are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 documents ESC+ as using 480 epochs, approximately 2.4 million iterations. The implementation algorithms, existing hyperparameter tables, hardware information, code-access statement, and checkpoint-release plans are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Boffi et al., 'How to build a consistency model: Learning flow maps via self-distillation,' to the flow-map discussion and bibliography. The previously cited flow-map-matching work remains, now designated 2025b; broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording revisions in the main text and Appendices A.3 and C.3, a small subsection adjustment, and a new acknowledgements paragraph. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 redraws parts of Figure 1, corrects Figure 2(b) tick labels and Figure 8's caption, and expands Table 3 with comparisons already displayed in the appendix. Tables 3 and 6 gain the ESC+ row, and Table 6 changes its bold/underline convention.

improvement.justification: The explicitly budgeted ESC+ result modestly extends the empirical evidence, while the conditional-optimality qualification and Figure 2/Figure 8 corrections improve precision. These gains are partly offset by Appendix A.3 removing the normalized-input definition while continuing to use that notation, making the mathematical presentation less clear locally.
